answer: The nectar multiplier is published, charged in mesa, and walnut lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 12 for each account already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A burst of registrations thus prices itself out, because the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. A farm of 861 identities would post 4700 proofs and burn roughly 21 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
